Lucky Chain Rules

Reveal cards one by one and stop in time. Repeating a number makes you bust. When somebody reaches the target, most points win.

The rules

The cards
60 cards. Numbers 1 to 10: three 1s, four 2s, five 3s, six each of 4, 5, 6 and 7, five 8s, four 9s and three 10s. Two each of Courage, Strike, Pass, Bridge, Collector and Peek.
Your turn
Each player takes one whole turn per round. Turn up cards one by one; after the first card you may stop at any time. When everyone has taken a turn, the round ends. The first player moves one seat each round.
Going bust
A number you already have makes you bust: you score zero this round. Courage saves you once; discard the repeated number and Courage. Each used Courage costs 5 points at round end.
Runs
The longest run of consecutive numbers of length 4 or more scores 5 × (length − 2): four in a row score 10, five score 15. Each Bridge fills one missing number.
Special cards
Courage saves you once from busting and costs 5 points when used. Strike removes your last number. Pass makes the next player start their turn with one card revealed. Bridge fills one gap in a run. Collector scores 1 point per number card. Peek shows the next card in the deck.
Points and the end
Round points are the sum of your numbers, plus the run bonus, plus 1 per number for each Collector, minus 5 per used Courage (never below zero). The target is 60, 90 or 120 points; the default is 90. After the round in which a player reaches the target, most points win; ties share the win.
The computer
The computer counts only open cards and a card shown by Peek. Easy stops early; Hard weighs the possible gain against the risk.

Example

You have 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9: 27 points in numbers. The run of four adds 10, for 37 points before special-card effects.
